To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of net C sequestrated and the price required to match a business-as-usual baseline varied widely across seven forest management carbon offset project protocols.

(1) the amount of carbon (C), or net C sequestrated, by a hypothetical forest management carbon offset project varies widely among seven of the protocols used to account for C sequestration, and (2) the price of C required to make the net present value (NPV) of the project equal to that of the non-project alternative varies widely among the seven protocols.

1) the amount of net carbon sequestration claimed by a carbon offset project can vary greatly depending on which of the many existing protocols is used, and 2) the cost of carbon sequestration is also affected by the protocol used.

the influence that accounting methods have on the amount of C claimed by forest management C offset protocols and the resulting cost implications for project development.
the question of how accounting rules and requirements influence the potential for C sequestration in forest management projects.
the influence of accounting protocols on C offset project costs.

the accounting scheme used to track the C offset from a project can have a significant influence on the amount of C sequestered, the cost of sequestration and the net C sequestrated.

forest management carbon offset project protocols can have significant impacts on project outcomes, and that project developers and land managers should consider the implications of these impacts before committing to a particular protocol.

forest management projects will likely be more costly than estimated by previous national analyses.

the accounting rules of a given protocol are likely to influence the net C sequestrations that a project can claim, the C price needed to make a project viable, and the overall cost of forest management C offset projects.

the choice of protocol can significantly influence the C storage estimates for individual forest management projects and thus the costs of implementing them.
